groups.distinction: Generated view handle/typed context distinguish caller-specific and anonymous native authority, while Vec/Option row results differ from RawQuery<T>. Explicit primary-key metadata has schema registration purpose; native typechecking is not proof of game-row invariants.
groups.uses: View macro checks context/return and preserves ordinary body for Vec/Option; Query converts to explicit raw SQL boundary. Generated FnInfo selects ViewKind<Ctx> and rejects scheduling views via FnKindView.
groups.disposition: Keep native context, query/row and generated handle distinctions. Do not make shared data owner depend on a particular observer permission merely to reuse wire storage; application projection boundaries still require own11 read. No macro execution or generated-source hand edits.
groups.acceptance: Any application schema/owner change preserves exact authority and row/query representation through native adapters; body excerpt only, no unregistered macro helper credit.

groups.distinction: Timestamp denotes signed microseconds since Unix epoch; Duration and TimeDuration are elapsed offsets with different signed/range guarantees. This distinction prevents treating a database instant as a game elapsed interval even without stricter positive numeric validation.
groups.uses: Explicit since-unix conversions preserve sign, before-epoch returns Err(Duration) as actual native signed-side adapter; native arithmetic routes through checked method then unwrap for operator. Display calls RFC3339 path, not arbitrary game-minute formatting.
groups.disposition: Keep clock/unit/instant-versus-duration distinctions. StrategicMinute, native timestamp and tactical duration must not unify solely for i64/u64 storage. No extra unsupported positive-epoch policy. Arithmetic extrema behavior belongs actual callers/operations, not rationale to collapse owner.
groups.acceptance: Later app clock adapters must state epoch, scale, sign and authority, preserve supported before-epoch inputs at real native boundary and avoid substituting wall clock for authored strategic/tactical time. No system-time conversion tail96+ or execution credited.

groups.distinction: Queued reducer invocation returns SDK Result<()> independently of later callback Result<Result<(),String>,InternalError>. Native status distinguishes commit, domain rejection and module panic. RequestID binds callback to reducer; generic typed TableHandle<Row> belongs local cache and module schema.
groups.uses: invoke_reducer_with_callback queues PendingMutation and returns Ok before send/commit. Later success applies update before callback; failure returns rejection or internal error. ParsedMessage transaction decode failures are SDK Error, distinguished from reducer result. get_table clones cache/channel and table identity, not synchronous remote fetch.
groups.disposition: Keep admission/queueing/commit and domain-versus-internal failure distinctions in application owners. Do not widen every outcome to generic String or treat dispatch Ok as committed. No extra wrapper needed merely for each nested Result if a native result remains at actual adapter; concrete application actor/status owner should prevent real mix-ups.
groups.acceptance: Actual application gateway/reducer consumers independently pending11: preserve callback request association, committed update visibility and rejection/dispatch/timeout semantics where present. No running subscription/cache, malformed-message acceptance, universal rollback guarantee or implicit table fetch claimed.

limits: Exact pinned registered ranges personally read for11; no other-lens source credit, source edits, tests/checks, native execution, clearance or implementation plan.
